info.name: HR Policy RAG Assistant
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Spring Boot HR Policy RAG backend.

All 10 endpoints are generated from the actual controllers:
- ChatController      -> POST /api/chat, POST /api/chat/stream
- DocumentController  -> POST /api/documents/upload, DELETE /api/documents/all
- DebugController     -> GET /api/debug/search, /api/debug/search-raw, /api/debug/stats
- Actuator            -> GET /actuator/health, /actuator/info, /actuator/metrics

## Before you run
1. Ollama must be listening on 11434 with `llama3` and `nomic-embed-text` pulled.
2. Postgres+pgvector must be up: `docker-compose up -d` (host port 5433).
3. Start the app: `mvn spring-boot:run`

## Suggested order
Run folder 0 (health) -> folder 1 (upload) -> folder 2 (verify retrieval) -> folder 3 (full RAG).
If documents are already ingested you can skip folder 1 entirely.

## Note on timing
Requests in folder 3 take 5-30s. The first call is slowest because Ollama must load llama3 (4.7 GB) into memory.

variable.description: App base URL. Change here once instead of editing every request.
Path to the PDF used by the upload request, relative to the repository root. Defaults to the tracked synthetic sample. Postman may require you to re-select the file manually via the Body tab.

variable.value: How many casual leaves do I get per year?

item.name: 0. Health & Info
item.description: Actuator endpoints. Exposure is controlled by `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,metrics` in application.yml — no other actuator endpoint is reachable over HTTP.

request.description: Build/app info. Returns an empty object {} unless you add `info.*` properties to application.yml or enable the build-info Maven goal — an empty body here is normal, not an error.

Lists available metric names. Drill into one by appending it, e.g. /actuator/metrics/http.server.requests or /actuator/metrics/hikaricp.connections.active (useful for spotting connection-pool exhaustion during bulk ingestion).

item.name: 1. Document Ingestion
item.description: Upload PDFs and clear the vector store. This is the 'write' side of the RAG pipeline: PDF -> text (PDFBox) -> chunks -> embeddings (nomic-embed-text) -> pgvector.

formdata.description: The form-field name MUST be exactly 'file' — it is bound by @RequestParam("file") MultipartFile in DocumentController. Any other name returns 400.

request.description:
POST /api/documents/upload  (consumes multipart/form-data)

Do NOT set Content-Type manually — Postman generates the multipart boundary for you. Adding the header by hand breaks the request.

Pipeline triggered by this call:
1. PdfTextExtractor  — PDFBox Loader.loadPDF + PDFTextStripper
2. TextChunkingService — chunk-size 1000 chars, overlap 50
3. EmbeddingModel — one 768-dim vector per chunk via Ollama /api/embed
4. VectorStore.add — INSERT into vector_store

Response (UploadResponse): fileName, totalCharacters, totalChunks, message, plus timing.

CAVEAT — there is no dedup on documentName. Uploading the same PDF twice stores two full copies of every chunk, and both copies then compete in retrieval. Run 1.2 first if you are re-ingesting.

Scanned/image-only PDFs extract to empty text (no OCR in this project) and will fail rather than silently store nothing.

DELETE /api/documents/all

DESTRUCTIVE — deletes every row in vector_store via chunkRepository.deleteAllChunks(). There is no per-document delete and no confirmation step. After this you must re-upload every PDF and re-embed, which costs a fresh embedding call per chunk.

Use it when: you changed chunk-size/overlap, switched embedding models, or accidentally double-ingested.

Response: {"deletedChunks": N, ...}

item.name: 2. Retrieval Debug (no LLM)
item.description: Inspect the RETRIEVAL half of RAG without paying for a slow LLM call. When an answer looks wrong, always check here first — it tells you whether the problem is retrieval (wrong/no chunks) or generation (right chunks, bad answer).

request.description:
GET /api/debug/stats

Returns what is stored plus the settings in force:
- totalChunks, documentCount, documents[]
- defaultTopK, similarityThreshold   (confirms a config change took effect)
- citationMode                       (which citation strategy is active)
- systemPrompt, userPromptTemplate    (the two messages that mode sends)

The cheapest way to answer 'is anything actually ingested?' — run this before debugging a bad answer.

query.description: REQUIRED. Bound by @RequestParam("q") — the param name is 'q', not 'query'. Omitting it returns 400.
Optional. Omitted, the configured app.retrieval.default-top-k applies (5 by default); GET /api/debug/stats reports the value in force.

request.description:
GET /api/debug/search?q=...&topK=...

Embeds your query, runs a cosine-similarity search against pgvector, and returns DebugSearchResponse:
- query
- embeddingDimensions      (must be 768 — mismatch means wrong embedding model)
- retrievedChunks[]         (text + score + document + chunkIndex + metadata)
- systemPrompt              (role and rules; identical every request)
- generatedPrompt           (the user message: context plus the question)
- citationMode              (which pair of templates the messages came from)
- structuredOutputSchema    (appended to the user message at call time; null unless model-attributed)
- searchParams              (the topK and similarityThreshold actually applied)

`systemPrompt` carries the role and rules; `generatedPrompt` is the user message. Together they are exactly what POST /api/chat sends, so it shows how the rules and retrieved context are assembled and roughly how much context you are spending. In model-attributed mode it carries [S1]/[S2] source labels.

Page numbers are inside each chunk's `metadata`, not on the chunk itself.

Omit topK to use the configured default. Invalid input returns 400: blank q, topK outside 1-20, or a non-numeric topK.

If retrievedChunks is empty, the threshold filtered everything out — compare with 2.3.

query.description: Optional. Omitted, the configured app.retrieval.default-top-k applies (5 by default).
Optional. Pre-filled at 0.3 here to demonstrate a stricter sweep; omit it and the configured app.retrieval.similarity-threshold applies (0.1), the same value 2.2 uses.

request.description:
GET /api/debug/search-raw?q=...&topK=...&threshold=...

Same search as 2.2, but executed as hand-written SQL against pgvector rather than through VectorStore, and the similarity threshold is a request parameter you can sweep without restarting the app. This is the tool for calibrating `app.retrieval.similarity-threshold`.

Try threshold=0.0 (everything), 0.3, then 0.7 (very strict) on the same query and watch how many chunks survive. Too low admits irrelevant chunks that waste context window; too high starves the LLM and produces 'I could not find this information'.

Also returns sqlExecuted — the real statement, placeholders intact — with sqlParameters explaining each binding.

Omit threshold and topK and it applies the same configured defaults as 2.2, so the two are directly comparable: identical rankings are expected, and a difference points at the abstraction rather than the data. Validation matches 2.2, plus threshold must be 0.0-1.0.

item.name: 3. Full RAG Chat
item.description: The complete retrieve -> augment -> generate pipeline. Slow by design (5-30s): step 3 blocks on llama3 inference inside Ollama.

request.description:
POST /api/chat

Body: ChatRequest { question (required, @NotBlank), topK (optional, @Min 1 / @Max 20) }

Omitting topK returns null from ChatRequest.requestedTopK(), and RetrievalService then applies app.retrieval.default-top-k — 5 in application.yml. That keeps the default in one place; check GET /api/debug/stats to see the value in force.

Response (ChatResponse): answer, sources (document plus page numbers), retrievedChunks with similarity scores, chunk count, processingTimeMs.

If the answer is 'I could not find this information in the HR policies provided' even though 2.2 returned good chunks, the prompt may be exceeding the context window: num-ctx is set to 8192 under spring.ai.ollama.chat.options, and a prompt that together with num-predict exceeds it is truncated from the front, where the role and grounding rules sit, before the retrieved context that follows them. Lower topK or raise num-ctx.

exec: console.warn('Fallback answer returned — check /api/debug/search first, then num-ctx.');

request.description:
Same endpoint with topK pinned explicitly.

Raise it (try 15) and run back-to-back against 3.1, which uses the configured default of 5: more chunks means a longer prompt, slower inference, and more risk of blowing the context window — but a lower chance the answer-bearing chunk was never retrieved. This trade-off is the core tuning knob of RAG.

item.name: 3.3 Validation Error — topK out of range (expect 400)

request.description:
NEGATIVE TEST — topK=25 violates @Max(20) on ChatRequest.

Flow: @Valid triggers Hibernate Validator -> MethodArgumentNotValidException -> GlobalExceptionHandler -> 400 with the message 'topK must be at most 20'. No LLM call is made, so this returns instantly.

Expected: 400, NOT 200.

NEGATIVE TEST — @NotBlank rejects null, empty, and whitespace-only strings. A body of {"question": "   "} is therefore invalid even though the field is present.

Expected: 400 with 'Question must not be blank'.

POST /api/chat/stream

Same body and validation as 3.1, but the answer arrives token by token as Server-Sent Events. Postman shows each event live in the response pane as it arrives.

Events (every data payload is JSON):
- retrieval: requestId, question, chunksRetrieved, retrievedChunks — sent before generation starts
- token: { text } — the next piece of the answer
- done: sources, processingTimeMs
- error: requestId, message — generation failed part way; the text so far is incomplete

Sources are decided after the answer. Under app.citations.mode=model-attributed, once the last token is sent a second structured model call reports which retrieved sources the answer came from, and each is verified against those supplied; expect done a few seconds after the last token. Under retrieval-scoped, every retrieved page is cited without that call. Nothing verified -> sources lists every retrieved page. A refusal -> sources is empty.

A stream running past app.streaming.timeout (150s) ends with an error event.

exec: const doneLine = body.split('\n').find((line, i, lines) => line.startsWith('data:') && lines[i - 1] === 'event:done');
